audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for servant oath, hand-under-thigh formula, kinship marriage search, chesed/emet prayer, Rebekah's actions and consent, blessing formula, and Isaac/Rebekah meeting. Long narrative chapter kept complete with focused notes.

verses.restored: Abraham was old, advanced in days, and the Eternal had blessed Abraham in everything.

familiar.text: And Abraham was old, and well stricken in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.

modern.text: By now Abraham was old and well along in years, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.

original.text: וְאַבְרָהָ֣ם זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַֽיהוָ֛ה בֵּרַ֥ךְ אֶת אַבְרָהָ֖ם בַּכֹּֽל

verses.restored: Abraham said to his servant, elder of his house, who ruled over all that was his, Place your hand under my thigh.

familiar.text: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house... Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:

notes.title: Hand under thigh
notes.body: An oath gesture tied to lineage/body. The exact ritual background is debated.

modern.text: So Abraham instructed the chief servant of his household, who managed all he owned, “Place your hand under my thigh,

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶל עַבְדּוֹ֙ זְקַ֣ן בֵּית֔וֹ הַמֹּשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר ל֑וֹ שִֽׂים נָ֥א יָדְךָ֖ תַּ֥חַת יְרֵכִֽי

verses.restored: I will make you swear by the Eternal, the Divine of the heavens and the Divine of the earth, that you will not take a woman for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I dwell.

familiar.text: And I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth...

modern.text: and I will have you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I am dwelling,

original.text: וְאַשְׁבִּ֣יעֲךָ֔ בַּֽיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: But you shall go to my land and to my kindred, and take a woman for my son Isaac.

familiar.text: But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.

modern.text: but will go to my country and my kindred to take a wife for my son Isaac.”

original.text: כִּ֧י אֶל אַרְצִ֛י וְאֶל מוֹלַדְתִּ֖י תֵּלֵ֑ךְ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֖ה לִבְנִ֥י לְיִצְחָֽק

verses.restored: The servant said to him, Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Shall I return your son to the land from which you came?

familiar.text: And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the woman will not be willing to follow me...

notes.title: Woman’s willingness
notes.body: The servant raises the possibility that the woman may not consent to come.

modern.text: The servant asked him, “What if the woman is unwilling to follow me to this land? Shall I then take your son back to the land from which you came?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הָעֶ֔בֶד אוּלַי֙ לֹא תֹאבֶ֣ה הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה לָלֶ֥כֶת אַחֲרַ֖י אֶל הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את הֶֽהָשֵׁ֤ב אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת בִּנְךָ֔ אֶל הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר יָצָ֥אתָ מִשָּֽׁם

verses.restored: Abraham said to him, Guard yourself, lest you return my son there.

familiar.text: And Abraham said unto him, Beware thou that thou bring not my son thither again.

modern.text: Abraham replied, “Make sure that you do not take my son back there.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו אַבְרָהָ֑ם הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֔ פֶּן תָּשִׁ֥יב אֶת בְּנִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: The Eternal, the Divine of the heavens, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my kindred, who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, To your seed I will give this land, he will send his messenger before you, and you shall take a woman for my son from there.

familiar.text: The LORD God of heaven, which took me from my father's house...

notes.title: Messenger before you
notes.body: Abraham trusts divine guidance ahead of the servant’s journey.

modern.text: The LORD, the God of heaven, who brought me from my father’s house and my native land, who spoke to me and promised me on oath, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give this land’—He will send His angel before you so that you can take a wife for my son from there.

original.text: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לְקָחַ֜נִי מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִי֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ מֽוֹלַדְתִּי֒ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּר לִ֜י וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִֽשְׁבַּֽע לִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַ֨רְעֲךָ֔ אֶתֵּ֖ן אֶת הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את ה֗וּא יִשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכוֹ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֛ה לִבְנִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם

verses.restored: But if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you shall be free from this oath of mine. Only do not return my son there.

familiar.text: And if the woman will not be willing to follow thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath...

notes.title: Consent condition repeated
notes.body: If the woman will not come, the servant is released. Isaac is not to be taken back.

modern.text: And if the woman is unwilling to follow you, then you are released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there.”

original.text: וְאִם לֹ֨א תֹאבֶ֤ה הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ וְנִקִּ֕יתָ מִשְּׁבֻעָתִ֖י זֹ֑את רַ֣ק אֶת בְּנִ֔י לֹ֥א תָשֵׁ֖ב שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: The servant placed his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.

familiar.text: And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master...

modern.text: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore an oath to him concerning this matter.

original.text: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם הָעֶ֨בֶד֙ אֶת יָד֔וֹ תַּ֛חַת יֶ֥רֶךְ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׁ֣בַֽע ל֔וֹ עַל הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: The servant took ten camels from the camels of his master and went, with every good thing of his master in his hand. He rose and went to Aram-Naharaim, to the city of Nahor.

familiar.text: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master...

modern.text: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed with all manner of good things from his master in hand. And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח הָ֠עֶבֶד עֲשָׂרָ֨ה גְמַלִּ֜ים מִגְּמַלֵּ֤י אֲדֹנָיו֙ וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל ט֥וּב אֲדֹנָ֖יו בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֗קָם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל אֲרַ֥ם נַֽהֲרַ֖יִם אֶל עִ֥יר נָחֽוֹר

verses.restored: He made the camels kneel outside the city by the well of water, at evening time, the time when women who draw water go out.

familiar.text: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water...

modern.text: As evening approached, he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town at the time when the women went out to draw water.

original.text: וַיַּבְרֵ֧ךְ הַגְּמַלִּ֛ים מִח֥וּץ לָעִ֖יר אֶל בְּאֵ֣ר הַמָּ֑יִם לְעֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב לְעֵ֖ת צֵ֥את הַשֹּׁאֲבֹֽת

verses.restored: He said, Eternal, Divine of my master Abraham, please make it happen before me today, and show covenant-kindness to my master Abraham.

familiar.text: And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day...

notes.title: Covenant-kindness
notes.body: Chesed is loyal, covenantal kindness. The servant prays for guided success as kindness to Abraham.

modern.text: “O LORD, God of my master Abraham,” he prayed, “please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.

original.text: וַיֹּאמַ֓ר יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם הַקְרֵה נָ֥א לְפָנַ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וַעֲשֵׂה חֶ֕סֶד עִ֖ם אֲדֹנִ֥י אַבְרָהָֽם

verses.restored: Look, I am standing by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

familiar.text: Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city...

modern.text: Here I am, standing beside the spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water.

original.text: הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב עַל עֵ֣ין הַמָּ֑יִם וּבְנוֹת֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֔יר יֹצְאֹ֖ת לִשְׁאֹ֥ב מָֽיִם

verses.restored: Let the young woman to whom I say, Please lower your jar so I may drink, and who says, Drink, and I will also water your camels, be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I shall know that you have shown covenant-kindness to my master.

familiar.text: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say...

notes.title: Hospitality test
notes.body: The sign sought is active generosity beyond the request: water for the servant and camels.

modern.text: Now may it happen that the girl to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and who responds, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. By this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.” Rebekah Is Chosen

original.text: וְהָיָ֣ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֹמַ֤ר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ הַטִּי נָ֤א כַדֵּךְ֙ וְאֶשְׁתֶּ֔ה וְאָמְרָ֣ה שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַם גְּמַלֶּ֖יךָ אַשְׁקֶ֑ה אֹתָ֤הּ הֹכַ֨חְתָּ֙ לְעַבְדְּךָ֣ לְיִצְחָ֔ק וּבָ֣הּ אֵדַ֔ע כִּי עָשִׂ֥יתָ חֶ֖סֶד עִם אֲדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: Before he had finished speaking, look, Rebekah came out, who had been born to Bethuel son of Milcah, woman of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, and her jar was on her shoulder.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out...

modern.text: Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי ה֗וּא טֶרֶם֮ כִּלָּ֣ה לְדַבֵּר֒ וְהִנֵּ֧ה רִבְקָ֣ה יֹצֵ֗את אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֻלְּדָה֙ לִבְתוּאֵ֣ל בֶּן מִלְכָּ֔ה אֵ֥שֶׁת נָח֖וֹר אֲחִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וְכַדָּ֖הּ עַל שִׁכְמָֽהּ

verses.restored: The young woman was very good in appearance, a virgin, and no man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up.

familiar.text: And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her...

modern.text: Now the girl was very beautiful, a virgin who had not had relations with any man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up again.

original.text: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ טֹבַ֤ת מַרְאֶה֙ מְאֹ֔ד בְּתוּלָ֕ה וְאִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א יְדָעָ֑הּ וַתֵּ֣רֶד הָעַ֔יְנָה וַתְּמַלֵּ֥א כַדָּ֖הּ וַתָּֽעַל

verses.restored: The servant ran to meet her and said, Please let me sip a little water from your jar.

familiar.text: And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Let me, I pray thee, drink a little water...

modern.text: So the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me have a little water from your jar.”

original.text: וַיָּ֥רָץ הָעֶ֖בֶד לִקְרָאתָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הַגְמִיאִ֥ינִי נָ֛א מְעַט מַ֖יִם מִכַּדֵּֽךְ

verses.restored: She said, Drink, my lord. She hurried and lowered her jar to her hand and gave him a drink.

familiar.text: And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher...

modern.text: “Drink, my lord,” she replied, and she quickly lowered her jar to her hands and gave him a drink.

original.text: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שְׁתֵ֣ה אֲדֹנִ֑י וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתֹּ֧רֶד כַּדָּ֛הּ עַל יָדָ֖הּ וַתַּשְׁקֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: When she finished giving him a drink, she said, I will also draw for your camels until they have finished drinking.

familiar.text: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also...

modern.text: After she had given him a drink, she said, “I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.”

original.text: וַתְּכַ֖ל לְהַשְׁקֹת֑וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר גַּ֤ם לִגְמַלֶּ֨יךָ֙ אֶשְׁאָ֔ב עַ֥ד אִם כִּלּ֖וּ לִשְׁתֹּֽת

verses.restored: She hurried and emptied her jar into the trough, ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.

familiar.text: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough...

notes.title: Rebekah’s agency
notes.body: The narrative emphasizes Rebekah’s quick, active generosity.

modern.text: And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw water, until she had drawn water for all his camels.

original.text: וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתְּעַ֤ר כַּדָּהּ֙ אֶל הַשֹּׁ֔קֶת וַתָּ֥רָץ ע֛וֹד אֶֽל הַבְּאֵ֖ר לִשְׁאֹ֑ב וַתִּשְׁאַ֖ב לְכָל גְּמַלָּֽיו

verses.restored: The man was gazing at her in silence, to know whether the Eternal had made his journey successful or not.

familiar.text: And the man wondering at her held his peace, to wit whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous...

modern.text: Meanwhile, the man watched her silently to see whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.

original.text: וְהָאִ֥ישׁ מִשְׁתָּאֵ֖ה לָ֑הּ מַחֲרִ֕ישׁ לָדַ֗עַת הַֽהִצְלִ֧יחַ יְהוָ֛ה דַּרְכּ֖וֹ אִם לֹֽא

verses.restored: When the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold nose-ring weighing a beka and two bracelets for her arms weighing ten shekels of gold.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking...

modern.text: And after the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring weighing a beka, and two gold bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר כִּלּ֤וּ הַגְּמַלִּים֙ לִשְׁתּ֔וֹת וַיִּקַּ֤ח הָאִישׁ֙ נֶ֣זֶם זָהָ֔ב בֶּ֖קַע מִשְׁקָל֑וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֤י צְמִידִים֙ עַל יָדֶ֔יהָ עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מִשְׁקָלָֽם

verses.restored: He said, Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?

familiar.text: And said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee...

modern.text: “Whose daughter are you?” he asked. “Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ בַּת מִ֣י אַ֔תְּ הַגִּ֥ידִי נָ֖א לִ֑י הֲיֵ֧שׁ בֵּית אָבִ֛יךְ מָק֥וֹם לָ֖נוּ לָלִֽין

verses.restored: She said to him, I am the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.

familiar.text: And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah...

modern.text: She replied, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו בַּת בְּתוּאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי בֶּן מִלְכָּ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֖ה לְנָחֽוֹר

verses.restored: She also said to him, We have plenty of straw and feed, and also room to spend the night.

familiar.text: She said moreover unto him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.

modern.text: Then she added, “We have plenty of straw and feed, as well as a place for you to spend the night.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו גַּם תֶּ֥בֶן גַּם מִסְפּ֖וֹא רַ֣ב עִמָּ֑נוּ גַּם מָק֖וֹם לָלֽוּן

verses.restored: The man bowed and worshiped the Eternal.

familiar.text: And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the LORD.

modern.text: Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD,

original.text: וַיִּקֹּ֣ד הָאִ֔ישׁ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַֽיהוָֽה

verses.restored: He said, Blessed be the Eternal, Divine of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned covenant-kindness and truth toward my master. As for me, the Eternal has led me on the way to the house of my master’s brothers.

familiar.text: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham...

notes.title: Covenant-kindness and truth
notes.body: Chesed ve-emet means loyal kindness and truth/faithfulness.

modern.text: saying, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא עָזַ֥ב חַסְדּ֛וֹ וַאֲמִתּ֖וֹ מֵעִ֣ם אֲדֹנִ֑י אָנֹכִ֗י בַּדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ נָחַ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אֲחֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: The young woman ran and told her mother’s house about these things.

familiar.text: And the damsel ran, and told them of her mother's house these things.

modern.text: The girl ran and told her mother’s household about these things.

original.text: וַתָּ֨רָץ֙ הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ וַתַּגֵּ֖ד לְבֵ֣ית אִמָּ֑הּ כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.

familiar.text: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban...

modern.text: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he rushed out to the man at the spring.

original.text: וּלְרִבְקָ֥ה אָ֖ח וּשְׁמ֣וֹ לָבָ֑ן וַיָּ֨רָץ לָבָ֧ן אֶל הָאִ֛ישׁ הַח֖וּצָה אֶל הָעָֽיִן

verses.restored: When he saw the nose-ring and the bracelets on his sister’s arms, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus the man spoke to me, he came to the man; and look, he was standing by the camels at the spring.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he saw the earring and bracelets...

modern.text: As soon as he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and heard Rebekah’s words, “The man said this to me,” he went and found the man standing by the camels near the spring.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י כִּרְאֹ֣ת אֶת הַנֶּ֗זֶם וְֽאֶת הַצְּמִדִים֮ עַל יְדֵ֣י אֲחֹתוֹ֒ וּכְשָׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֞י רִבְקָ֤ה אֲחֹתוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה דִבֶּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל הָאִ֔ישׁ וְהִנֵּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עַל הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים עַל הָעָֽיִן

verses.restored: He said, Come in, blessed of the Eternal. Why do you stand outside? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.

familiar.text: And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the LORD...

modern.text: “Come, you who are blessed by the LORD,” said Laban. “Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בּ֖וֹא בְּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה לָ֤מָּה תַעֲמֹד֙ בַּח֔וּץ וְאָנֹכִי֙ פִּנִּ֣יתִי הַבַּ֔יִת וּמָק֖וֹם לַגְּמַלִּֽים

verses.restored: The man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels. Straw and feed were given to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.

familiar.text: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels...

modern.text: So the man came to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and feed were brought to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of his companions.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָאִישׁ֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַיְפַתַּ֖ח הַגְּמַלִּ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֨ן תֶּ֤בֶן וּמִסְפּוֹא֙ לַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וּמַ֨יִם֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ רַגְלָ֔יו וְרַגְלֵ֥י הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Food was set before him to eat, but he said, I will not eat until I have spoken my words. He said, Speak.

familiar.text: And there was set meat before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat...

modern.text: Then a meal was set before the man, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told you what I came to say.” So Laban said, “Please speak.”

original.text: ויישם לְפָנָיו֙ לֶאֱכֹ֔ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֹכַ֔ל עַ֥ד אִם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי דְּבָרָ֑י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽר

verses.restored: He said, I am Abraham’s servant.

familiar.text: And he said, I am Abraham's servant.

modern.text: “I am Abraham’s servant,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אָנֹֽכִי

verses.restored: The Eternal has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great. He has given him flocks, herds, silver, gold, male servants, female servants, camels, and donkeys.

familiar.text: And the LORD hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great...

modern.text: “The LORD has greatly blessed my master, and he has become rich. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, menservants and maidservants, camels and donkeys.

original.text: וַיהוָ֞ה בֵּרַ֧ךְ אֶת אֲדֹנִ֛י מְאֹ֖ד וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל וַיִּתֶּן ל֞וֹ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וְכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וַעֲבָדִם֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים

verses.restored: Sarah, my master’s woman, bore a son to my master after she was old, and he has given him all that is his.

familiar.text: And Sarah my master's wife bare a son to my master when she was old...

modern.text: My master’s wife Sarah has borne him a son in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns.

original.text: וַתֵּ֡לֶד שָׂרָה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת אֲדֹנִ֥י בֵן֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י אַחֲרֵ֖י זִקְנָתָ֑הּ וַיִּתֶּן לּ֖וֹ אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לֽוֹ

verses.restored: My master made me swear, saying, You shall not take a woman for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I dwell,

familiar.text: And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife...

modern.text: My master made me swear an oath and said, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I dwell,

original.text: וַיַּשְׁבִּעֵ֥נִי אֲדֹנִ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹא תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ

verses.restored: but you shall go to my father’s house and to my family, and take a woman for my son.

familiar.text: But thou shalt go unto my father's house, and to my kindred...

modern.text: but you shall go to my father’s house and to my kindred to take a wife for my son.’

original.text: אִם לֹ֧א אֶל בֵּית אָבִ֛י תֵּלֵ֖ךְ וְאֶל מִשְׁפַּחְתִּ֑י וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֖ה לִבְנִֽי

verses.restored: I said to my master, Perhaps the woman will not follow me.

familiar.text: And I said unto my master, Peradventure the woman will not follow me.

modern.text: Then I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not come back with me?’

original.text: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֶל אֲדֹנִ֑י אֻלַ֛י לֹא תֵלֵ֥ךְ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אַחֲרָֽי

verses.restored: He said to me, The Eternal, before whom I have walked, will send his messenger with you and make your way successful. You shall take a woman for my son from my family and from my father’s house.

familiar.text: And he said unto me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee...

modern.text: And he told me, ‘The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you may take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father’s house.

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י יְהוָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנָ֗יו יִשְׁלַ֨ח מַלְאָכ֤וֹ אִתָּךְ֙ וְהִצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתִּ֖י וּמִבֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי

verses.restored: Then you shall be free from my oath when you come to my family. If they do not give her to you, you shall be free from my oath.

familiar.text: Then shalt thou be clear from this my oath, when thou comest to my kindred...

modern.text: And when you go to my kindred, if they refuse to give her to you, then you will be released from my oath.’

original.text: אָ֤ז תִּנָּקֶה֙ מֵאָ֣לָתִ֔י כִּ֥י תָב֖וֹא אֶל מִשְׁפַּחְתִּ֑י וְאִם לֹ֤א יִתְּנוּ֙ לָ֔ךְ וְהָיִ֥יתָ נָקִ֖י מֵאָלָתִֽי

verses.restored: I came today to the spring and said, Eternal, Divine of my master Abraham, if now you are making successful the way on which I go,

familiar.text: And I came this day unto the well, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham...

modern.text: So when I came to the spring today, I prayed: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if only You would make my journey a success!

original.text: וָאָבֹ֥א הַיּ֖וֹם אֶל הָעָ֑יִן וָאֹמַ֗ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אִם יֶשְׁךָ נָּא֙ מַצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכִּ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י הֹלֵ֥ךְ עָלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: look, I am standing by the spring of water. Let the maiden who comes out to draw, to whom I say, Please give me a little water from your jar to drink,

familiar.text: Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass...

modern.text: Here I am, standing beside this spring. Now if a maiden comes out to draw water and I say to her, ‘Please let me drink a little water from your jar,’

original.text: הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב עַל עֵ֣ין הַמָּ֑יִם וְהָיָ֤ה הָֽעַלְמָה֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣את לִשְׁאֹ֔ב וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י אֵלֶ֔יהָ הַשְׁקִֽינִי נָ֥א מְעַט מַ֖יִם מִכַּדֵּֽךְ

verses.restored: and who says to me, You drink, and I will also draw for your camels—let her be the woman whom the Eternal has appointed for my master’s son.

familiar.text: And she say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels...

modern.text: and she replies, ‘Drink, and I will draw water for your camels as well,’ may she be the woman the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.

original.text: וְאָמְרָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ גַּם אַתָּ֣ה שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַ֥ם לִגְמַלֶּ֖יךָ אֶשְׁאָ֑ב הִ֣וא הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁר הֹכִ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה לְבֶן אֲדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, look, Rebekah came out, with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew, and I said to her, Please let me drink.

familiar.text: And before I had done speaking in mine heart, behold, Rebekah came forth...

modern.text: And before I had finished praying in my heart, there was Rebekah coming out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. So I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’

original.text: אֲנִי֩ טֶ֨רֶם אֲכַלֶּ֜ה לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל לִבִּ֗י וְהִנֵּ֨ה רִבְקָ֤ה יֹצֵאת֙ וְכַדָּ֣הּ עַל שִׁכְמָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֥רֶד הָעַ֖יְנָה וַתִּשְׁאָ֑ב וָאֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ הַשְׁקִ֥ינִי נָֽא

verses.restored: She hurried and lowered her jar from upon her shoulder and said, Drink, and I will also water your camels. So I drank, and she also watered the camels.

familiar.text: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder...

modern.text: She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well.’ So I drank, and she also watered the camels.

original.text: וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתּ֤וֹרֶד כַּדָּהּ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַם גְּמַלֶּ֖יךָ אַשְׁקֶ֑ה וָאֵ֕שְׁתְּ וְגַ֥ם הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים הִשְׁקָֽתָה

verses.restored: I asked her and said, Whose daughter are you? She said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him. Then I placed the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.

familiar.text: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou?...

modern.text: Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She replied, ‘The daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.’ So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.

original.text: וָאֶשְׁאַ֣ל אֹתָ֗הּ וָאֹמַר֮ בַּת מִ֣י אַתְּ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בַּת בְּתוּאֵל֙ בֶּן נָח֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָֽלְדָה לּ֖וֹ מִלְכָּ֑ה וָאָשִׂ֤ם הַנֶּ֨זֶם֙ עַל אַפָּ֔הּ וְהַצְּמִידִ֖ים עַל יָדֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: I bowed and worshiped the Eternal, and blessed the Eternal, Divine of my master Abraham, who led me in the true way to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.

familiar.text: And I bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD...

modern.text: Then I bowed down and worshiped the LORD; and I blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to take the granddaughter of my master’s brother for his son.

original.text: וָאֶקֹּ֥ד וָֽאֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה וָאֲבָרֵ֗ךְ אֶת יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִנְחַ֨נִי֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֱמֶ֔ת לָקַ֛חַת אֶת בַּת אֲחִ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י לִבְנֽוֹ

verses.restored: Now if you are acting with covenant-kindness and truth toward my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.

familiar.text: And now if ye will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me...

modern.text: Now if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; but if not, let me know, so that I may go elsewhere.”

original.text: וְ֠עַתָּה אִם יֶשְׁכֶ֨ם עֹשִׂ֜ים חֶ֧סֶד וֶֽאֱמֶ֛ת אֶת אֲדֹנִ֖י הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֑י וְאִם לֹ֕א הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֔י וְאֶפְנֶ֥ה עַל יָמִ֖ין א֥וֹ עַל שְׂמֹֽאל

verses.restored: Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The matter has gone out from the Eternal; we cannot speak to you bad or good.

familiar.text: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceedeth from the LORD...

modern.text: Laban and Bethuel answered, “This is from the LORD; we have no choice in the matter.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן לָבָ֤ן וּבְתוּאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵיְהוָ֖ה יָצָ֣א הַדָּבָ֑ר לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רַ֥ע אוֹ טֽוֹב

verses.restored: Look, Rebekah is before you. Take her and go, and let her become the woman of your master’s son, as the Eternal has spoken.

familiar.text: Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go...

modern.text: Rebekah is here before you. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, just as the LORD has decreed.”

original.text: הִנֵּֽה רִבְקָ֥ה לְפָנֶ֖יךָ קַ֣ח וָלֵ֑ךְ וּתְהִ֤י אִשָּׁה֙ לְבֶן אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself to the earth before the Eternal.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, when Abraham's servant heard their words...

modern.text: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֛ע עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַ֖רְצָה לַֽיהוָֽה

verses.restored: The servant brought out objects of silver, objects of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and to her mother.

familiar.text: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold...

modern.text: Then he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and he gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother.

original.text: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א הָעֶ֜בֶד כְּלֵי כֶ֨סֶף וּכְלֵ֤י זָהָב֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לְרִבְקָ֑ה וּמִ֨גְדָּנֹ֔ת נָתַ֥ן לְאָחִ֖יהָ וּלְאִמָּֽהּ

verses.restored: They ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and spent the night. They rose in the morning, and he said, Send me away to my master.

familiar.text: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that were with him...

modern.text: Then he and the men with him ate and drank and spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, he said, “Send me on my way to my master.”

original.text: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֗וּ ה֛וּא וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר עִמּ֖וֹ וַיָּלִ֑ינוּ וַיָּק֣וּמוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שַׁלְּחֻ֥נִי לַֽאדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: Her brother and her mother said, Let the young woman stay with us days, perhaps ten; afterward she may go.

familiar.text: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days...

modern.text: But her brother and mother said, “Let the girl remain with us ten days or so. After that, she may go.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָחִ֨יהָ֙ וְאִמָּ֔הּ תֵּשֵׁ֨ב הַנַּעֲרָ֥ אִתָּ֛נוּ יָמִ֖ים א֣וֹ עָשׂ֑וֹר אַחַ֖ר תֵּלֵֽךְ

verses.restored: He said to them, Do not delay me, since the Eternal has made my way successful. Send me away, so that I may go to my master.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my way...

modern.text: But he replied, “Do not delay me, since the LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so that I may go to my master.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַל תְּאַחֲר֣וּ אֹתִ֔י וַֽיהוָ֖ה הִצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכִּ֑י שַׁלְּח֕וּנִי וְאֵלְכָ֖ה לַֽאדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: They said, Let us call the young woman and ask her mouth.

familiar.text: And they said, We will call the damsel, and enquire at her mouth.

notes.title: Ask her mouth
notes.body: Rebekah’s own answer is requested. This is a crucial consent moment in the narrative.

modern.text: So they said, “We will call the girl and ask her opinion.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ נִקְרָ֣א לַֽנַּעֲרָ֑ וְנִשְׁאֲלָ֖ה אֶת פִּֽיהָ

verses.restored: They called Rebekah and said to her, Will you go with this man? She said, I will go.

familiar.text: And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.

notes.title: I will go
notes.body: Rebekah gives direct consent and chooses immediate departure.

modern.text: They called Rebekah and asked her, “Will you go with this man?” “I will go,” she replied.

original.text: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ לְרִבְקָה֙ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ הֲתֵלְכִ֖י עִם הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וַתֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֵֽךְ

verses.restored: They sent away Rebekah their sister, her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his men.

familiar.text: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse...

modern.text: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.

original.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת רִבְקָ֥ה אֲחֹתָ֖ם וְאֶת מֵנִקְתָּ֑הּ וְאֶת עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְאֶת אֲנָשָֽׁיו

verses.restored: They blessed Rebekah and said to her, Our sister, may you become thousands of ten-thousands, and may your seed possess the gate of those who hate him.

familiar.text: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands...

notes.title: Rebekah blessing
notes.body: The family blessing echoes the seed/gate promise language spoken over Abraham’s line.

modern.text: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.”

original.text: וַיְבָרֲכ֤וּ אֶת רִבְקָה֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לָ֔הּ אֲחֹתֵ֕נוּ אַ֥תְּ הֲיִ֖י לְאַלְפֵ֣י רְבָבָ֑ה וְיִירַ֣שׁ זַרְעֵ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת שַׁ֥עַר שֹׂנְאָֽיו

verses.restored: Rebekah and her young women rose, rode on the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah and went.

familiar.text: And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels...

modern.text: Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left. Isaac Marries Rebekah

original.text: וַתָּ֨קָם רִבְקָ֜ה וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֗יהָ וַתִּרְכַּ֨בְנָה֙ עַל הַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וַתֵּלַ֖כְנָה אַחֲרֵ֣י הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיִּקַּ֥ח הָעֶ֛בֶד אֶת רִבְקָ֖ה וַיֵּלַֽךְ

verses.restored: Isaac had come from the way of Beer-lahai-roi, and he was dwelling in the land of the Negev.

familiar.text: And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahairoi...

notes.title: Beer-lahai-roi
notes.body: The well associated with Hagar reappears near Isaac’s story.

modern.text: Now Isaac had just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, for he was living in the Negev.

original.text: וְיִצְחָק֙ בָּ֣א מִבּ֔וֹא בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י וְה֥וּא יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַנֶּֽגֶב

verses.restored: Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening. He lifted his eyes and saw, and look, camels were coming.

familiar.text: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide...

notes.title: Meditate
notes.body: The verb suach is rare; meditate, stroll, or muse are possible.

modern.text: Early in the evening, Isaac went out to the field to meditate, and looking up, he saw the camels approaching.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק לָשׂ֥וּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִפְנ֣וֹת עָ֑רֶב וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה גְמַלִּ֖ים בָּאִֽים

verses.restored: Rebekah lifted her eyes and saw Isaac, and she dismounted from the camel.

familiar.text: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off the camel.

modern.text: And when Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she got down from her camel

original.text: וַתִּשָּׂ֤א רִבְקָה֙ אֶת עֵינֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֖רֶא אֶת יִצְחָ֑ק וַתִּפֹּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל הַגָּמָֽל

verses.restored: She said to the servant, Who is that man walking in the field to meet us? The servant said, He is my master. So she took the veil and covered herself.

familiar.text: For she had said unto the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us?...

modern.text: and asked the servant, “Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?” “It is my master,” the servant answered. So she took her veil and covered herself.

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל הָעֶ֗בֶד מִֽי הָאִ֤ישׁ הַלָּזֶה֙ הַהֹלֵ֤ךְ בַּשָּׂדֶה֙ לִקְרָאתֵ֔נוּ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הָעֶ֖בֶד ה֣וּא אֲדֹנִ֑י וַתִּקַּ֥ח הַצָּעִ֖יף וַתִּתְכָּֽס

verses.restored: The servant recounted to Isaac all the things that he had done.

familiar.text: And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.

modern.text: Then the servant told Isaac all that he had done.

original.text: וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר הָעֶ֖בֶד לְיִצְחָ֑ק אֵ֥ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה

verses.restored: Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother. He took Rebekah, and she became his woman, and he loved her. Isaac was comforted after his mother.

familiar.text: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah...

notes.title: Sarah’s tent
notes.body: Rebekah enters Sarah’s tent, symbolically moving into the matriarchal place after Sarah’s death.

notes.title: He loved her
notes.body: Love is explicitly named in Isaac and Rebekah’s union.

modern.text: And Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah and took Rebekah as his wife. And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.

original.text: וַיְבִאֶ֣הָ יִצְחָ֗ק הָאֹ֨הֱלָה֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֧ח אֶת רִבְקָ֛ה וַתְּהִי ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וַיֶּאֱהָבֶ֑הָ וַיִּנָּחֵ֥ם יִצְחָ֖ק אַחֲרֵ֥י אִמּֽוֹ
